description:
12,000 strangers. Different countries. Never met. All describe the same tall man in a wide-brimmed hat watching them sleep. Skeptics blame brain chemistry — but some witnesses were fully awake. Here are the 3 most disturbing documented Hat Man cases, including a nurse in Ohio and a truck driver in Texas.

0:00 The figure 12,000 strangers describe
2:55 Why skeptics blame brain chemistry
4:05 The problem with the hallucination theory
5:21 Case 1: the truck driver in Texas
6:51 Case 2: the nurse in Ohio
8:34 Case 3: the sketch drawn from memory
9:22 What is he?

My take: the sleep-paralysis explanation is too neat. Random brain glitches should produce random monsters — not the same hat, the same coat, the same watching figure across continents. The awake witnesses are what keep me up at night.

If this one got under your skin, tell me in the comments: have you ever seen him?

title: He Haunts 12,000 Sleepers and They All Describe Him
